title: Finite-field and $p$-adic Planck dynamics
html:
Remark. Finite-field and p-adic Planck dynamics

The Planck step t_P(q) = q/(q-1) (discrete Planck step) is a rational function of q. Both t_P(q) and the iteration f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) realise over any field. We record the finite-field and p-adic incarnations of the Planck dynamics.

Finite-field dynamics. Over k = \mathbb{F}_\pp with q \in \mathbb{F}_\pp^\times, the iteration f_q \colon \mathbb{F}_\pp \to \mathbb{F}_\pp acts on a finite set. Every orbit is eventually periodic. This orbit structure encodes the Planck dynamics of the finite-field QOU:

  • Orbit length |O_x| counts the Planck steps before state x recurs. This provides the finite-field analogue of Poincaré recurrence time.
  • Fixed points of f_q satisfy z^2 - z + c(q) = 0. They exist in \mathbb{F}_\pp if and only if 1 - 4c(q) is a quadratic residue modulo \pp.
  • Period-n orbits are roots of f_q^{\circ n}(z) = z not fixed by any f_q^{\circ d} for d \mid n. The Weil zeta function of the curve w^2 = z^2 + c(q) over \mathbb{F}_\pp governs their count.

The Julia set J(f_q) over \mathbb{C} complexifies this finite orbit structure. The boundary between escaping and bounded orbits provides the continuous analogue to partitioning \mathbb{F}_\pp into short-period and long-period orbits.

p-Adic Planck step. Over \mathbb{Q}_\pp, the substrate parameter q carries a \pp-adic valuation. The Planck time t_P = q/(q-1) has valuation v_\pp(t_P) = v_\pp(q) - v_\pp(q-1). When q \equiv 1 \pmod{\pp^n}, q approaches the classical limit in the \pp-adic topology. Here v_\pp(q-1) \geq n. The Planck time becomes \pp-adically large, dictating slow dynamics. When v_\pp(q-1) = 0, q occupies the Big Bang regime. The Planck time reaches minimal valuation, dictating maximally fast dynamics.

The Witt vector lift (Witt vector lift) promotes the \mathbb{F}_\pp orbit structure to a \mathbb{Z}_\pp-lattice. The finite orbits of f_q over \mathbb{F}_\pp lift to Teichmüller representatives in \mathbb{Z}_\pp. The \pp-adic Planck step acts on these lifts via the Frobenius endomorphism. The passage \mathbb{F}_\pp \to \mathbb{Q}_\pp \to \mathbb{C} forms the arithmetic analogue of cosmological progression, moving from the discrete Big Bang to the continuous classical limit.
